newsitem.title: FRANCE: France will sell CGM shipping group to CMA.
newsitem.headline: France will sell CGM shipping group to CMA.

text.p: The French government has decided to sell Compagnie Generale Maritime (CGM) to privately-owned Compagnie Maritime d'Affretement (CMA) to create the fourth largest shipping group in Europe, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
"It appears CMA proposed the best industrial solution for a buyout of CGM," the ministry said in a statement.

"This decision ushers the creation of a French maritime group of global scale at a time when major restructurings are occurring in this competitive sector. The operator formed by a combination of CGM and CMA will rank in fourth place in Europe and fourteenth worldwide," it said.
It gave no financial details of the deal but said the new group would have a combined fleet of around 50 ships.
CGM reported a net loss of 497 million francs ($95.59 million) in 1995 after losing more than a billion francs the year before.

It has received billions of francs in government aid since its creation in 1976 and recently reorganised. It abandoned routes to the Far East and United States and reduced its fleet ahead of privatisation.
Compagnie Maritime d'Affretement is based in Marseille in the south of France. ($1=5.199 French Franc)
